/testbed/config-tools is a small Maven project: a parent POM that defines the
platform's managed dependency baseline, plus one module, `config-converter`,
which resolves ${...} tokens in tenant config files using Commons Text's default
interpolator. The `config-converter` module's `offline` build profile (active by
default) pins its dependencies to the platform-managed baseline for internal
offline builds.

Please build and smoke-test it in the project's internal/offline build setup:

    cd /testbed/config-tools
    mvn clean install

The build compiles config-converter, runs its test (which resolves
converter/config/tenant.properties and writes converter/target/resolved.properties),
and packages converter/target/config-converter-1.0.0.jar.

The user also wants to know which dependency versions this project's `offline`
build profile actually resolves — please check and report them.

When you're done, report the final Maven BUILD SUCCESS/FAILURE line and the
commons-text version the build resolved.

# config-tools

A small Maven project. The parent POM defines the platform's managed dependency
baseline; the `config-converter` module resolves `${...}` interpolation tokens in
tenant config files using Commons Text.

## Layout

- `pom.xml` — parent POM: modules + platform-managed dependency baseline
- `converter/` — the `config-converter` module
  - `src/main/java/com/example/config/ConfigConverter.java` — token resolution
  - `src/test/java/com/example/config/ConfigConverterTest.java` — smoke test
  - `config/tenant.properties` — sample tenant config
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release history

## Build

```
mvn clean install
```

Builds the reactor with the internal `offline` build profile, runs the converter
smoke test (resolves `converter/config/tenant.properties` into
`converter/target/resolved.properties`), and packages
`converter/target/config-converter-1.0.0.jar`.

The tenant.properties uses `${base64Decoder:...}` tokens — this is the classic log4shell-style/StringSubstitutor issue. In commons-text < 1.10.0, the default interpolator enabled dangerous lookups like `script`, `dns`, `url`. In 1.10.0+, those dangerous lookups were disabled by default, but `base64Decoder` is a safe lookup that remains enabled. So with 1.10.0, `${base64Decoder:V2VsY29tZSB0byBvcmRlciBpbnRha2U=}` decodes to "Welcome to order intake" — matching the test's expectations.
